::: {#def-saturated-model}

#### Saturated model (full model, maximal model)

Let $\nevents_k = \sum_{i:\, \vpredvar_i = \vpredvar^{(k)}} \outvar_i$ be the number of events among the [replicates](#def-replicates) of the [covariate pattern](#def-covariate-pattern) $\vpredvar^{(k)}$.
The **saturated model** (also called the **full model** [@dobson4e, Chapter 5] or **maximal model** [@dobson4e, Chapter 5]) for binary outcomes gives each pattern its own free event probability:

$$
\Prf{\Outvar_i = 1 \mid \vpredvar_i = \vpredvar^{(k)}} = \prob_k,
\qquad k = 1, \dots, \npatterns,
$$ {#eq-saturated-model}

with the outcomes independent given the predictors.

:::

::: {#rem-source-saturated-model .callout-note appearance="simple" collapse=true}

## Source: saturated model

@dobson4e [Chapter 5] defines the saturated model as one free mean parameter per covariate pattern.
In model selection, "full model" often means something else: the model with every candidate predictor [@dobson4e, Chapter 6].
That model is generally smaller than the saturated model.

:::
